ENT Clinical Note

Subjective:
- Presenting complaint and trigger/exposure:
  • 26-y-o female with 3-day history of progressively worsening “crazy” headache; no clear external trigger identified.
- Symptom timeline and progression:
  • Started gradually at work ≈3 days ago; constant baseline with intermittent surges in intensity.  
  • Severity now 8/10; ibuprofen 3 tablets/day for 2 days provided no relief.
- ENT symptoms:
  • Throat swelling/closure sensation: denied.  
  • Voice change/hoarseness: denied.  
  • Dysphagia/odynophagia & drooling: denied.  
  • Nasal symptoms: no congestion, rhinorrhea, or sinus pressure reported.  
  • Ocular: photophobia; transient “shooting lights” at onset; no true visual loss.  
  • Stridor/noisy breathing, dyspnea: denied.  
  • Facial/lip/tongue/uvular swelling: denied.  
  • Ear pain/hearing changes: denied.  
  • Neck pain/stiffness: denied.  
  • Other neurologic: nausea (no vomiting), difficulty concentrating; no weakness, speech changes, or sensory loss.
- Relevant past episodes and treatments:
  • Prior headaches responsive to NSAIDs; no previous migraine diagnosis; no ED visits/hospitalizations.
- Allergies and current medications:
  • Drug/food allergies: none known.  
  • Current meds: Ibuprofen 200 mg? (exact strength not documented) 3 tabs/day x 2 days; glasses for myopia (device). No regular prescriptions.
- Social context:
  • Lives with three housemates; works full-time in IT (heavy screen use); social smoker and social alcohol use; mild project-related stress.

Objective:
- Observable swelling and distribution: none reported.
- Airway/breathing: no stridor, dyspnea, or voice change noted.
- Mental status: alert, appropriate; reports difficulty focusing secondary to pain.
- Vitals and examination findings: Not recorded (tele-consultation).
- Presence of another person: not specified.

Assessment:
- Working impression: Probable migraine (possible aura) vs tension-type headache.
  Evidence: unilateral-predominant pain around right eye, photophobia, visual scintillations, moderate–severe intensity, nausea, strong family history of migraine, lack of response to low-dose NSAID.
- DDx (aligned with DDx JSON):
  1. Migraine with/without aura – high likelihood; fits symptom profile and family history.
  2. Tension-type headache – moderate likelihood; diffuse dull component and work stress support; photophobia less typical.
  3. Acute frontal/ethmoid sinusitis – low likelihood; right-eye pain but absence of nasal/fever symptoms argues against.
  No conflicting data between transcript and DDx.

Plan:
- Pharmacologic:
  • Educated patient that ibuprofen dose can be increased to 400 mg (two 200 mg tablets) up to TID with meals if tolerated.  
  • Will prescribe stronger NSAID (Naproxen 500 mg BID, exact script to be issued) ± add-on paracetamol or codeine as required for breakthrough pain.
- Non-pharmacologic:
  • Keep headache diary (date, time, intensity, possible triggers) until review.  
  • Adjust screen brightness, ensure regular breaks, maintain hydration, manage stress.
- Follow-up:
  • Routine follow-up in 1–2 weeks; sooner if headaches become more frequent or refractory.  
  • Discuss preventive (prophylactic) therapy at next visit if ≥4 disabling headaches/month.
- Escalation / red-flags:
  • Seek urgent care (call EMS/attend ED) for sudden severe “worst ever” headache, visual loss, limb weakness, speech changes, vomiting, fever, neck stiffness, or altered consciousness.

Quality checks (document_quality):
● Missing/expected: vitals, detailed neuro & ENT exam, exact ibuprofen strength, documentation of OTC dosing advice compliance, formal visual acuity/field assessment, allergy verification, menstrual/OCP history (risk for IIH or CVST).  
● Conflicts: none between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: clear; minimal filler; no significant inaudible sections.
